description: Inventory of committed test evidence in tests/. Each family is classified as: fence (re-runnable test that compares against stored result), partial-fence (harness exists but not wired to CI comparison), archive (historical measurements, not re-runnable), or delete (no current claim supported).

families.claim: Language-detection performance comparison for go-enry v0.6.0 reader optimization.
families.reason: Performance measurements are hardware-dependent; results would differ on any other machine. The optimization is already shipped. The 66 MB evidence.tar.gz and 48 MB audit.json are the largest items in the repository.

families.claim: Intermediate measurements for the library release candidate.
Stress-test run results (large-scale scan timings and RSS measurements).
families.reason: Stress results are hardware-dependent and not deterministic.

families.claim: CPU and memory profiles from scanner optimization investigations.
families.reason: Raw profiling data from a specific host; no re-runnable claim.

families.claim: Per-version performance comparisons (wall time and RSS) for released candidates.
families.note: tests/performance/bounded_reader/ has a Python test harness (test_*.py) that verifies the harness format but does NOT re-run the performance measurement. The per-version subdirectories (v040_candidate, v050_candidate, …) are archives.

families.claim: Archive-smoke and compatibility checks for released versions.
families.note: tests/release/test_*.py runs in CI (preflight job) but checks harness structure, not live binary output.

families.claim: Compatibility matrix between v0.3.0 and current candidate.
families.note: test_harness.py runs in CI preflight. run.py + verify.py re-run against a candidate binary but are not currently called in CI. The canonical/ subdirectory holds the reviewed golden expectations.

families.claim: context-aware analysis receipt contracts for v0.8.0.
families.note: test_receipts.py runs in CI preflight and verifies receipt integrity.

families.claim: Composition-check golden results for a synthetic C#/Java fixture.
families.note: canonical/ holds verified golden expectations. run.py re-runs against a candidate binary+worker and produces new results. verify_schema.py validates the schema. Neither is called in CI. The schema_test.go.txt overlay IS run in ci via make check.
make conformance runs in CI (linguist-conformance job). Results uploaded as artifacts.
Referenced by compatibility_next but not independently tested in CI.

phase_1_before_public.description: Move the three largest evidence families to release assets or a separate git-lfs-tracked evidence branch. These must happen while history rewrite is cheap (before the repository goes public).

items.action: Attach to v0.6.0 release as an asset named 'enry-performance-evidence-final.tar.gz'. Remove from history with git-filter-repo. Keep the README.md and manifest JSON in-tree.
Attach to v0.6.0 release as an asset. Remove from history.
Attach to the library-rc1 pre-release or to v0.6.0. Remove from history.
Archive to a tagged release artifact; remove from repository history.
Archive to a tagged release artifact; remove from repository history.

phase_2_rolling_compatibility.description: After going public: consolidate the per-version compatibility directories into a single rolling harness.
items: The rolling harness downloads checksum-pinned released binaries, runs them on the fixture, and compares with reviewed golden expectations.
Each released version's expectations are a small JSON file; the binary is downloaded on demand and cached.
